question: Does the declared finite relational geometry already contain or canonically generate the rank-one P-to-N partial isometry required by claim 1544?

declaredData.realCompletion: J supplies the adjoint/conjugate orientation and anticommutes with relation-sheet parity

anchoredClassification.meaning: anchors select one complex line but no normalized vector or phase

boundary: polar normalization divides by |y| and is undefined at y=0
the phase is inherited from the chosen Majorana block
projectors and anchors alone do not generate this element

symmetryAudit.J: pairs t_phi with its adjoint/conjugate orientation but admits every phi
symmetryAudit.CP: restricts phi to 0 or pi but does not choose the sign

relationSheet.phaseSelection: none; parity is constant over each supported line

branchConditioning.safeConstruction: b_D tensor E_PP plus b_M tensor Sym(t_phi E_PP)
branchConditioning.warning: realizing the coefficient identification by an actual D-to-M carrier map invokes claim 1521's forbidden cross-anchor enlargement

coefficientBoundary.rawBlock: imports independent magnitude |y| and phase arg(y)
coefficientBoundary.polarBlock: removes |y| but retains relative phase exp(-i arg(y))

minimumReopeningDatum.required: one relation-sheet-even branch-conditioned phase-and-coefficient locking law between the Dirac PP coefficient line and the polar Majorana PN line
acceptableForms: a natural transformation iota_M = Sym(v_M composed with iota_D)
a gauge-invariant closed relation cycle fixing the relative phase
minimumReopeningDatum.forbiddenImplementation: a carrier operator sewing the Dirac and Majorana wheels

verdict: The allowed Majorana relation already supplies a unique complex P-to-N matrix-unit line and a nonzero Majorana D block supplies a conditional polar representative. The declared anchors, J, CP and relation-sheet parity do not select its phase or enforce use of that representative to transport the Dirac coefficient. The forbidden Dirac P-N one-form stays absent.
